newsitem.title: USA: Calif. measure would bar closed-door budget talks.
newsitem.headline: Calif. measure would bar closed-door budget talks.

text.p: A California state assemblyman said Friday he would introduce a resolution to bar back-room budget negotiations by the governor and legislative leaders.
Assemblyman Don Perata, a freshman Democrat, said he would introduce his resolution at Monday's Assembly rules committee meeting.
The resolution would bar closed-door meetings of the so-called "Big Five," a group that includes senior legislative leaders and Gov. Pete Wilson.
The Big Five typically meets in private to negotiate a budget compromise. The budget that emerges is then sent to floors of the Senate and Assembly for enactment.
Critics charge that the Big Five usurps the authority of the Senate and Assembly to negotiate the budget.
"The reasons for instituting the Big Five budget negotiations no long exist. The governor is now using the process to usurp legislative initiative," Perata said.
